content.value_statement: Data rights registration requires coordinated evidence, technical review, and ongoing deadline management. This skill structures the process and prepares practical draft materials.
actual_capabilities: Assesses basic registration readiness using ownership, source, privacy, classification, and applicant information.
Distinguishes initial, transfer, amendment, renewal, and cancellation registration scenarios.
Organizes an initial registration package against a 12-item material checklist.
Drafts outlines for technical review reports and examination inquiry responses.
Creates registration ledgers with certificate details, expiry dates, and renewal reminders.
limitations: It does not issue official registration decisions or guarantee acceptance.
It does not replace advice or signatures from licensed lawyers and qualified review organizations.
Local requirements vary, so users must confirm current rules with the selected registration authority.
Its policy knowledge may require verification against newer laws, standards, and agency guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan an Initial Registration
use_cases.description: Assess readiness, identify evidence gaps, and build a sequenced application checklist.

use_cases.title: Answer an Examination Inquiry
use_cases.description: Map each authority question to supporting evidence, responsible owners, and a draft response.

use_cases.title: Manage Renewals and Changes
use_cases.description: Create a registration ledger and schedule renewal, transfer, or amendment actions.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Required Materials
prompt_templates.prompt: We plan an initial data rights registration. List the information you need, then provide a 12-item preparation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Registration Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this data resource for registration readiness: [details]. Separate confirmed facts, evidence gaps, legal review needs, and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Inquiry Response
prompt_templates.prompt: The authority raised these questions: [questions]. Draft a response matrix with proposed answers, evidence, owners, and unresolved risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Registration Control Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an end-to-end control plan for [portfolio]. Include registration types, approval gates, evidence standards, ledger fields, renewal triggers, and escalation rules.

output_examples.input: We want to register a customer analytics dataset created from licensed transaction records.
output: Priority evidence: source licenses, permitted processing scope, personal information handling, and dataset boundaries.
Next step: legal review before technical report preparation.

output_examples.input: The authority says our data source evidence and scope description are insufficient.
output: Source evidence: attach contracts, authorization records, and collection process documentation.
Scope description: define fields, time range, record volume, update frequency, and exclusions.
Response control: cite each attachment and assign an accountable document owner.

output_examples.input: Create a renewal plan for certificates expiring next year.
output_examples.output: The plan groups certificates by expiry date, starts review three months early, assigns owners, and records renewal evidence and status.

best_practices: Verify every factual claim against source documents and label assumptions clearly.
Confirm the selected authority's current forms, fees, review rules, and submission channel.
Route legal conclusions and formal opinions to qualified counsel before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not treat registration as proof that all underlying rights are valid.
Do not submit personal, important, or core data without completing required compliance checks.
Do not invent certificate codes, authority decisions, legal citations, or supporting evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill submit applications?
faq.answer: No. It prepares plans and drafts, while the user submits through the applicable authority.

faq.question: Does registration guarantee ownership?
faq.answer: No. Registration may provide public evidence, but underlying rights and legal defects still require independent review.

faq.question: Can it prepare a legal opinion?
faq.answer: It can organize facts and draft an outline. A qualified lawyer must review and issue any formal legal opinion.

faq.question: Which registration types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers initial, transfer, amendment, renewal, and cancellation registration workflows.

faq.question: How does it handle regional differences?
faq.answer: It identifies questions to verify, but users must confirm current local authority requirements.

faq.question: Can it track expiry dates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design a ledger and renewal schedule, but it does not run reminders by itself.
